entities.title: Plays the same, looks new
entities.summary: Every rule, number, timing and random draw of RULES is kept; every word, name, layout, model and sound is LodeStar's own.
entities.statement: The sim implements docs/RULES.md exactly, including the order of random draws and the deliberate differences it lists, while the galaxy data, market, names, text and art are new.
entities.rationale: A player of the 1984 game should recognise every system and make the same decisions, while nothing of the original's protected expression is copied.
acceptanceCriteria: Unit tests check each rule as RULES writes it
Data-swapped parity traces replay bit for bit through FlyInSystem::tick
The overlap check over docs/ and the text table is clean

origin.description: GDD § 2, pillar 1; DESIGN § What retro gameplay means.

entities.title: You always see your own ship
entities.summary: A third-person orbit camera, space-anchored by default, with a limited zoom, is the one deliberate change to how the game plays.
entities.statement: The camera orbits the player's ship between 1.5× and 5× its length, holds its direction in space by default and can follow behind the active mount; the camera never changes what the sim does.
acceptanceCriteria: Orbiting and zooming never reach the sim

entities.title: Four laser mounts, the pilot picks the active one
entities.summary: Keys 1–4 choose the fore, aft, port or starboard mount; lasers fire, hit and lock only from it.
entities.statement: The active mount replaces the original's view switching: only its laser fires, its axis is the sights for hits and the missile lock, and the camera can swing to look along it.
acceptanceCriteria: A mount press changes the active mount once
Lasers fire only from the space view

entities.title: Save only at a station; death returns to the save
entities.summary: Saving happens only while docked, under a name, and death returns the pilot to the last save.
entities.statement: The pilot can save only while docked; death and starting from the title restore the last saved or loaded pilot, so every launch risks what was earned since.
acceptanceCriteria: Death returns to the saved copy

entities.title: A desktop game
entities.summary: Windows, macOS and Linux with a keyboard and mouse; no web build, no phones or touch.
entities.statement: LodeStar ships as a native desktop game: the Godot runtime with the exported game and the lodestar-godot library for each platform.
